andrew_sales: Heads-up — Prospect (FinBank) asked for a SIG/CAIQ follow-up focused on Access Control. They want concrete artifacts for SSO/SAML, MFA enforcement, RBAC role matrix, and service account practices. Can SE/security pack this by EOD? Attaching questionnaire excerpts below.

sam_se: On it. I'll gather SAML metadata, Okta policy screenshot, and a role mapping CSV. Do they need IdP-initiated or SP-initiated examples?

andrew_sales: Both would be ideal. Also they asked for evidence of least privilege for service accounts and audit logs retention.

maria_sre: For MFA: we enforce org-level MFA via Okta. We can provide policy screen: Settings > Security > MFA Policy (screenshot) and an exported Okta system log extract for a week (redacted PII).

jess_prod: RBAC: we have canonical roles (Owner, Admin, Engineer, Viewer, ServiceAccount). I'll export our role matrix from the console (/admin/roles/export.csv) and add brief descriptions + allowed actions per role.

sam_se: I'll prepare these items:
- redwood-saml-metadata.xml (SP metadata)
- okta-mfa-policy.png (screenshot)
- role_matrix.csv
- svc_account_guidelines.md (least-priv practices + example IAM policies)
- audit_log_sample.json (redacted)
I'll upload to presales bucket and share link.

andrew_sales: Perfect — make sure the filenames match what they list in the SIG attachments checklist (they often want specific filenames). Also include a short README that maps artifacts to SIG/CAIQ rows.

security_bot: Ticket CREATED: PRESALES-1129 assigned to sam_se, due 2026-03-21 17:00 UTC

sam_se: Uploaded to s3: s3://redwood-presales/finbank/sig-iam-evidence/
Commands I ran:
aws s3 cp redwood-saml-metadata.xml s3://redwood-presales/finbank/sig-iam-evidence/
aws s3 cp role_matrix.csv s3://redwood-presales/finbank/sig-iam-evidence/
aws s3 cp okta-mfa-policy.png s3://redwood-presales/finbank/sig-iam-evidence/

andrew_sales: Shared link to customer (private): https://redwood.internal/s3/finbank/sig-iam-evidence/ — sent.

alice_cust: Thanks, received. Quick Q: For service accounts, can you confirm automated rotation schedule and KMS usage?

maria_sre: Yes — service account credentials rotate on a 90-day schedule by default. We strongly encourage short-lived tokens where possible; our platform supports automatic key rotation and integration with KMS for envelope encryption. For Private deployments customers can supply their own customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). I'll add a short config snippet.

sam_se: Added svc_account_rotation.md and kms_diagram.svg to the bucket.

jess_prod: I'll draft a short cover note mapping each artifact to the SIG rows and CAIQ questions and drop it as README_SIG_mapping.md in the same location.

andrew_sales: Awesome — closing loop. If they ask about audit retention: default is 1 year for hosted, configurable longer for Dedicated/Private. Point them to compliance/log-retention.md for details.

alice_cust: Great, we'll review the artifacts with our vendor-risk team and loop back if anything else is required. Appreciate the quick turnaround.
